text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Central Election committee announced preliminary results of the municipal election. The total turnout was about 56.84 percent which is slightly less than the previous elections. In Riga Council the opposition Social Democrats have won 11 seats, with governing Fatherland & Freedom 10 seats, Latvia's Way has won nine and the Democratic Party Saimnieks five seats.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs said recent developments in the relations between Latvia and Russia signalled positive changes. There are four intergovernmental treaties under preparation now which are likely to be signed in April. Birkavs said the two countries were stable trade partners. Latvia's exports to Russia reached 22.8 percent of the total export volume in 1996.
- Parliament has again failed to pass a law on compulsory motor vehicle insurance as there was no quorum. It will continue discussions on March 13.
- Latvian Jewish youth commemorated the victims of the Holocaust at Rumbula, a place where Jews were massacred in 1941.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs has left for London to participate in an opening ceremony for Latvian students at London University. He will give a lecture on Latvian foreign policy priorities at London University.

- Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans says the treaty on air services between Latvia and Russia is likely to be signed in April. According to Krishtopans, it would help solve a long-standing dispute between the two countries on air traffic.

- The Latvian Development Agency and Latvian businesses are planning to open a Latvian Trade Centre in Moscow. The starting capital of the project is $1.3 million of which 150,000 lats may be taken from the state privatisation fund.
- Norwegian Varner Hakon Invest and Latvian company Skonto are to privatise Hotel Latvia, one of the biggest in Riga.
